title: Large-list scroll
scenario: A Grid (five single-line text columns) over a synthetic 100,000-row model (variant rows-1m: 1,000,000 rows), revealed at its middle row (variants default and rows-1m at 1280x720, fhd at 1920x1080, uhd-192dpi at 3840x2160 and 192 DPI), beside a Tree over a synthetic, fully expanded 10,000-row model; absolute layout, reduced motion. A hover phase moves the pointer between two Grid rows (20 frames); then each list is scrolled for 10 s of the frozen fixture clock at 120 Hz, one wheel notch down per frame (1,200 frames each). The models compute every row from its index and store none. G6 (missed frames) is a hardware timing verdict: not measured here; the receipt records the work of every scroll step and memory per row count.
drawCalls: not counted: frame.drawCalls is 0 without the counting wrappers

phases.name: warm
phases.description: reveal the middle row of the Grid; one wheel notch on the Grid and one on the Tree; two unchanged frames

phases.name: hover
phases.description: the pointer moves between two Grid rows 40 DIP apart: one hover change per frame

phases.name: grid
phases.description: the clock advances 8 or 9 ms (120 Hz) and one wheel notch down scrolls the Grid

phases.name: tree
phases.description: the clock advances 8 or 9 ms (120 Hz) and one wheel notch down scrolls the Tree

timing.reason: timing comes only from performance-timing.ps1 on a hardware adapter in a quiet window (W0.2); counts and memory are recorded here
